description.purpose: One generation of one person's agent, as a level. A level owns what its siblings must share, and what two channels of one assistant must share is exactly two things: the REASONING CORE they consult (cogny@4.0.3 -- a second opinion that answers as its own turn) and the TOOL SURFACE they call (tools@1.1.0 -- one node, one contract, `tool_call` in and `tool_result` out). Beside them sits one open container, `channels`, that the surfaces are instantiated into. Because that container is a node of THIS template, the fan-in edges between it and its two siblings are internal edges shipped once (GH #303) instead of per-instance wiring re-drawn for every channel.
description.use_when: One per generation. Instantiate it into a member's `assistants` container and wire its transit lanes in the same mutation; the hive is an island until an edge crosses into it. Channels come afterwards, one mutation per channel. A generation swap replaces this node and the older one stays in place, silent and readable -- which is why the memory, the identity and the screen are NOT here: they belong to the member, and a swap must not reset what the person is known to be.
description.not_in_scope: No memory hive, no identity store and no memory-drain: the memory belongs to the MEMBER (GH #122, ADR 0012), and per-turn extraction (GH #298, ruling Q11) replaced the drain -- `extraction` leaves this level on a lane of its own. No firewall: the screen sits outside the generation so that two channels of one person meet ONE view of an attacker and the rate window does not restart because a generation was replaced (GH #302). No terminal and no sink of any kind (ruling Q2, GH #284): `error` leaves the level and becomes no_route in the DLQ if nobody consumes it, which is recorded and self-localising. No tool schemas and no per-tool credentials -- a schema lives in the calling brain's `system.tools` and a credential in the cell that needs it. No connector and no talky shipped INSIDE the container: a channel is instantiated, never shipped.
examples: PORTS - the assistant is an OPEN hive: it declares no params.ports, because it is a level that gets wired INTO and sealing it would refuse exactly the endpoints a channel instantiation needs. Entry lanes, all six addressed at the assistant path itself: 'in_turn' (the screened turn coming back from the member's firewall -- promote context.channel, and context.audience_set if the closed sessions of this generation are to reach a memory), 'in_bundle' (the member's memory answer), 'in_advice' (a second agent's answer, arriving as its own turn), 'in_sweep', 'in_prune' and 'in_round_sweep' (operator housekeeping). Exits, all seven leaving the assistant path: 'turn' (an inbound turn on its way to the member's screen), 'write', 'turn_write', 'extraction' (to the member's memory hive in_remember door), 'recall', 'prune', 'error'. Two pairings are declared in params.required_drains: in_turn -> error and in_prune -> prune.

the container: ./channels is a real, empty, open hive. It declares NO contract of its own, and that is a rule of this wave rather than an omission: a container its own level wires is a WIRED hive from birth, so every lane it declared would owe a door INSIDE it, and an empty container has no inside -- the declaration would refuse every mutation of the colony until the first channel stands there. The lanes are declared by the level; the container's transit list is prose in its own description.

the unbound behaviour of ./channels is UNDECLARED, deliberately: GH #285's slot governs an address that does not exist, and this container does exist, so the declared word could never fire. A message that reaches it before a channel is instantiated takes the ordinary path. The measurement comes from unbound_slot_behaviour in crates/meclaw-colony/src/colony.rs, which steps aside as soon as the target is a registered hive scope.

the tool exit is ONE edge and it names no tool: ./channels -> ./tools is a single GUARDED DEFAULT on hop.route == 'tool'. The two consult errands (consult_cogny, ask_memory) are ordinary conditioned edges on hop.tool_name, so a consult fires a regular edge and the default stays silent, while a real tool call fires nothing regular and the default carries it. The exclusion chain that used to name every tool is gone entirely.

WHERE THE THIRTEEN LANES COME FROM: the union of what this level's occupants accept and emit at the versions pinned in each `because` (talky@4.2.2 and telegram-connector@2.0.0 inside ./channels, cogny@4.0.3, tools@1.1.0), minus the lanes a sibling inside the level consumes itself -- answer, tool, tool_call/tool_result and in_tool. If an occupant moves a lane, this level moves with it in the same commit: crates/meclaw-cells/tests/gh302_assistant_wires_channels_once.rs reads those files and fails until it does.

adding a second channel: one add_nodes into <assistant>/channels with the connector and the talky, plus the edges that pair them and the edges that carry the level's lanes down to that talky. It adds NO edge between ./channels and a sibling -- those eighteen are shipped with this template and drawn once.
